identity.description:
Replace the long-lived project lead after the hand-over with a watcher and small window sessions

## Summary

After a crew run hands over its PR, the project lead no longer stays alive with its whole build context. A watcher with no model now watches the PR, CI and the deploy at no token cost. When something lands that needs a model, such as a review, a comment, a failed check, the merge or a word from a person or an orchestrator, the watcher opens one small window session in a new tab. That session reads the run's record, handles the whole burst of events, writes the record and closes. Before this change, the window was 64% of a project lead's cost: every call there read a median 209K-token build context again, and a 30-minute watch expiry woke the session only to arm the watch again.

**Ticket:** N/A (orchestrator item window-session, no GitHub issue)
**Type:** New feature

## Agent context

### Authority

- `docs/design.md` §15.<TBD> (new finding, number assigned at merge).
- `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md` owns the window session and the project lead's hand-over; `skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md` the watcher's poll and cursor; `skills/delivered-window/references/patch-mode.md` (new) the patch rounds of a review's findings.
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md` owns `handover.md`, `window/` and `run.window`.
- `skills/project-lead/references/crew-step.md` owns the new `watch` step of `hand-over` and the new `verify` diff output.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md` owns `launcher.py window`.
- `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md` owns how the orchestrator reaches a delivered item (`say`).

### What changed, by file

- `skills/delivered-window/scripts/window-watch.py` (new): the watcher. `start [--hold]`, `release`, `ensure`, `stop`, `say`, `claim`, `next`, `done [--final]`, `status`. One detached process per delivered run; polls with `pr-watch.sh` every 60 s with no expiry; drops events that need no model (the run's own push and ready flip from `run.window.own`, `queued`, a passing check, the run's own comment); queues the rest durably and acks the cursor itself; waits 120 s of quiet (600 s cap) and starts one window session per burst through `launcher.py window`; one session slot per run; a launch is recorded before the launcher call and reconciled with `launcher.py find`; sets up the deploy on `merged` and polls it; flags a stale tab and asks the orchestrator.
- `skills/delivered-window/scripts/test-window-watch.sh` (new): 90 seeded checks with a stub `gh`, launcher, poll and `crew-orch.py`, and the real `crew-record.py`.
- `skills/delivered-window/scripts/watch-step.py`: the `Monitor` `arm` subcommand is gone; `deploy --setup-only` writes `run.deploy` and returns. `test-watch-step.sh` changed to match.
- `skills/delivered-window/scripts/pr-watch.sh`: the die message and the header name the watcher, not `Monitor`.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/launcher.py`: new `window --name --cwd --prompt-file [--model] [--group]` subcommand: one interactive tab, no worktree, no branch, prints one JSON line whose `tab` is the handle `stop` takes. `test-launcher.sh` has 13 new checks.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/crew-step.py`: `hand-over` runs `window-watch.py start --hold` in a new `watch` step after `orch`; `verify` now writes the package diff to `diffs/<package-id>-verify.patch` and prints its path and the stat, and `--diff` prints the whole diff. This run saw about 1,200 lines of diff in the `verify` output of one prose package. `test-crew-step.py` covers both; its R20 check now guards the `crew-record.py` command lines instead of the whole file.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/crew-record.py`: one exclusive lock per record around each read-modify-write, because the watcher and a session write the same record. `hooks/session-end.py` takes the same lock and no longer marks a `delivered` run interrupted.
- `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md`: rewritten for the window session (entry, the watcher's events, own acts, the gate that asks and ends, the deploy, the ship word with `done --final`, the hand-over); under 500 lines.
- `skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md`, `references/patch-mode.md` (new): the watcher's poll and cursor; the patch-mode procedure moved out of SKILL.md.
- `skills/review/SKILL.md`: a review run posts round 1, writes `handover.md`, starts the watcher and ends.
- `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`: the `Window model` standing-instruction section (default opus).
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md`: `handover.md` with its nine headings, `window/`, every `run.window` field, the record lock.
- `skills/project-lead/references/goal-check.md`, `simple-path.md`, `full-path.md`, `resume.md`, `skeptical-review.md`, `orchestrator-report.md`: the project lead ends at the hand-over with `window-watch.py release`; its own pushes and flips after `start` go to `run.window.own`; a resume runs `ensure`, `claim`, the owed work, `done`.
- `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md`, `references/resume-and-close.md`, `references/launcher.md`: the orchestrator sends the merge word, the rebase word and gate answers to a delivered item with `window-watch.py say --item`, and runs `ensure` on its resume.
- `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/design.md`: the new way, the layout rows, the build state and the finding.

### Constraints that applied

- "Only the launcher and `crew-usage.py` start a `claude` process" holds: the watcher starts a session only through `launcher.py window`.
- One rule in one file: the window session's rules live in `crew:delivered-window`; other files point at it. The writing-standard checklist was read for each changed instruction file; `SKILL.md` is 494 lines.
- Version and §15 number: left as placeholders for the orchestrator. The manifests are not bumped in this PR, and the finding is numbered `<TBD>`.
- The project lead never merges.

### How this was verified

Every seeded test passes on the branch head: `test-window-watch.sh` 90/90, `test-watch-step.sh` 90/90, `test-pr-reply.sh` 55/55, `test-pr-watch-deploy.sh` 23/23, `test-launcher.sh` 326/326, `test-crew-step.py` 177/177, `test-crew-stats.py` 26/26, `test-review-run.py` 140/140, `test-plan-review.py` 45/45, `test-crew-orch.sh` all, `test-crew-usage.py` 107/107. Each code package had a red commit that failed its new checks. A Codex plan review over all five plans found six blocking design faults (record write races, the cursor, burst recovery, the deploy set-up, the tab close order, and the session ownership on resume), and each was fixed before code.

Window size, before and after. Before, from the orchestrator's study of three weeks of transcripts: the window started at a median 209K tokens and made about 87 calls. After: the seeded test measures the first prompt plus every record file it names at 5,071 bytes. An estimate from file sizes (about 3.6 bytes a token over the study's 58K base): a notice session starts at about 72K tokens and makes about 10 calls; a patch round with an IC reaches about 110K to 120K and makes 30 to 40 calls. Events that need no model start no session.

### Known gaps

- No real window session has run. The token figures above are estimates, not a transcript measurement. One probe against a seeded record would measure them.
- A wait before the hand-over (a usage-limit pause, a question to the principal) still wakes the build context. The orchestrator made it a second item.
- A machine restart stops the watcher; `--resume` or the orchestrator's resume runs `ensure` to start it again. Nothing starts it at login.
- The test drives the watcher with a stub poll, so the real `pr-watch.sh` runs only in its own deploy test.
